verdict.reasoning: Patient reports: "terrible headaches since midday on the left side" and when asked if pain came on suddenly says "No, really, it just happened," indicating sudden onset since midday and severe left-sided pain.

Patient: "Yeah, I guess it's throbbing on that left side" and "if I lean forward or like move my head or neck. Yeah, the headache gets worse," confirming throbbing quality and worsening with movement such as leaning forward or moving head/neck.

Patient: "I noticed some zigzag lines in my vision. A few minutes before the headache started, my vision blurred"; when asked if vision issues are in one or both eyes, patient replies "It feels like it's on both," supporting visual aura with zigzag lines and bilateral blurred vision prior to headache.

Doctor asks: "Have you had any difficulty with seeing bright lights at all?" Patient: "Yeah, well, I'm wearing, wearing sunglasses right now. You know, light's really hurting my eyes," confirming photophobia and wearing sunglasses indoors.
Patient initially: "I just feel like I need to vomit"; later, Doctor: "Have you Vomited at all?" Patient: "Yeah, I vomited twice," confirming nausea and two episodes of vomiting.

Patient: "I did have a similar headache a few weeks ago"; lasted "For a couple of days"; "had to take painkillers and had to go to bed and rest and had a couple days off work," supporting prior similar episode a few weeks ago lasting about 2 days, improved with painkillers and rest, and required sick leave.
Doctor asks: "has anyone told you've had migraines in the past?" Patient: "No"; and adds "I've not been diagnosed," confirming no prior history of diagnosed migraines.

Doctor: "Have you noticed any problems with your speech at all?" Patient: "No." "Any problems with your arms and legs, for example, numbness or weakness?" Patient: "No." "Any difficulty with balance, your balance or coordination?" Patient: "No," confirming denial of these symptoms.

Doctor asks about "Any temperatures or fevers?" Patient: "No, I don't feel feverish." and "Any other funny skin rashes that you may have noticed?" Patient: "No"; "Have you had any injuries to your head?" Patient: "No," confirming no fever, rash, or head trauma.

Patient: "I've just been googling... if your headache gets worse when you move, it could be a sign of brain cancer" and "my friend's mum, she recently died of a brain tumor. So it's really concerning me" and "what if it is a brain tumor?" indicating main concern is fear of a brain tumor due to friend's mother dying of brain cancer.
Doctor: "Do you have any other medical history I should be aware of?" Patient: "No," supporting no reported past medical history.

Patient: "I take the pill, microgynon." Doctor: "And how long have you been on that for?" Patient: "Three months." Doctor: "And is that mainly for contraception... ?" Patient: "It's for contraception," matching the statement.
Patient: "My mum had. Has migraines" and "My mum has an underactive thyroid as well," supporting maternal migraines and hypothyroidism.

Patient: "working fashion industry" and "Yeah, it's really stressful, actually. Having problems with like people at work... managers like putting a lot of pressure on me," confirming fashion industry job and high stress.
Doctor: "Who's at home with you?" Patient: "I live on my own," confirming she lives alone.
Doctor: "Do you smoke at all?" Patient: "No." "And do you drink much in the way of alcohol?" Patient: "No," confirming denial of smoking and alcohol use.
Doctor: "Do you do much in the way of exercise?" Patient: "No," confirming low levels of exercise.

The transcript contains no mention of vital signs (e.g., BP, HR, temperature) or specific physical examination findings; only a comment that the doctor would like to proceed to examination, so noting that none are documented is accurate.

While the doctor screens for neurological symptoms, no physical neurological examination findings or focal deficits are documented in the transcript; thus stating no documented focal neurological deficit is accurate.

Doctor: "I wonder whether you may. May have a migraine. Migraine type headache. It sounds very classical of that nature. The headache on one side, throbbing nature, the nausea, vomiting, sensitive to bright lights." Prior similar episode and family history of migraines are also described, supporting a probable migraine assessment based on those features.

Patient repeatedly expresses worry: "I'm just really worried"; "I've read... it could be a sign of brain cancer"; "what if it is a brain tumor?" and doctor acknowledges "I can see your concerns." This supports anxiety about having a brain tumor.

Doctor: "Some strong painkillers would be advisable. So, you know, think about paracetamol or even cocodamol and some anti inflammatories such as ibuprofen and naproxen," matching the analgesia/NSAID advice.
Doctor: "I think keeping a headache diary will be quite important to see exactly what's triggering these headaches," confirming instruction to start a headache diary.

Doctor: "if your symptoms aren't getting better in the next two, three days, or indeed they're getting worse, I'd like you to come back and see me straight away" and references to worsening headache, neck pain, or development of weakness or vision problems, which are focal neurological symptoms, matching the safety-netting description.

Doctor: "if your headaches were to become more persistent, then we can maybe think about giving you some medications that will stop your headaches from happening in the first place. Something prophylactic medicines," supporting consideration of migraine prophylaxis if recurrence persists.
Doctor: "we can have a discussion next time I see you next week, perhaps," indicating intent for a follow-up appointment for discussion and reassessment.
As above, "next time I see you next week, perhaps" indicates planned follow-up for reassessment of the condition.
